questions.q: Which substring function spelling does T-SQL support, and which does Oracle support?
options: T-SQL only has SUBSTR; Oracle only has SUBSTRING
T-SQL only has SUBSTRING; Oracle only has SUBSTR
Neither supports substring extraction natively
Both support both spellings equally
questions.explain: T-SQL is SUBSTRING-only and Oracle is SUBSTR-only, while MySQL and PostgreSQL are generous enough to accept both spellings.

questions.q: What's the difference between MySQL's LENGTH() and CHAR_LENGTH()?
options: LENGTH returns byte length, CHAR_LENGTH returns character length
LENGTH only works on numbers, CHAR_LENGTH only works on strings
They are exact synonyms with no difference
CHAR_LENGTH is deprecated and should never be used
questions.explain: MySQL splits the concept: LENGTH counts bytes, CHAR_LENGTH counts characters — they diverge once multi-byte encodings are involved.

questions.q: What's the key difference in argument order between T-SQL's CHARINDEX and Oracle's INSTR?
options: INSTR doesn't accept a substring argument at all
CHARINDEX takes the substring first, then the string; INSTR takes the full string first, then the substring
They take arguments in the exact same order
CHARINDEX takes three arguments, INSTR takes only one
questions.explain: CHARINDEX(substring, string) and INSTR(string, substring) reverse the argument order — a common source of bugs when porting code.

questions.q: Which MySQL function matches T-SQL's CHARINDEX argument order (substring first)?
options: LENGTH(string)
INSTR(string, substring)
SUBSTR(string, start, length)
LOCATE(substring, string)
questions.explain: MySQL's LOCATE takes the substring first, matching CHARINDEX's order, while MySQL's INSTR matches Oracle's string-first order instead.

questions.q: Which string operation is consistent, by name and behavior, across T-SQL, Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL?
options: TRIM / LTRIM / RTRIM
SUBSTRING / SUBSTR
CHARINDEX / INSTR / LOCATE / POSITION
LEN / LENGTH / CHAR_LENGTH
questions.explain: Trimming functions (TRIM, LTRIM, RTRIM) are the one area with genuine consistency across all four dialects covered in this course.
